one_line: A pediatric ER nurse (per the account name) speaks to camera in a selfie shot next to a stroller whose hood is covered in a white cloth, warning parents that covering a stroller with fabric in hot weather can dehydrate a child, and asking viewers to send it to friends.

hook.visual: Selfie-style shot on a street: a woman in maroon scrubs with a colourful lanyard speaks and gestures; behind her a stroller has a white muslin-style cloth draped over the whole hood.
hook.on_screen_text: השבוע הגיע אמא / למיון עם ילדה (This week a mom came to the ER with a girl)
hook.first_spoken_line: בוא יגיע אמא למיון עם ילדה מאוד מאוד מיובשת, אדומה, מזיעה ובאמת עם התייבשות. (Whisper; the burned-in caption reads 'השבוע הגיע אמא למיון', so likely 'This week a mom came to the ER with a very, very dehydrated girl, red, sweating, and truly dehydrated.')
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: A first-person clinical story from someone in scrubs ('this week in the ER') with a frightening outcome, while the covered stroller behind her is something many parents recognise from their own routine.

beats.observed: Nurse in scrubs and lanyard speaks and gestures at the camera; the cloth-covered stroller sits behind her and stays in frame for the whole video. Black-box caption highlights track her words.
beats.spoken: A mom came to the ER with a very dehydrated, red, sweating girl, truly dehydrated (Whisper, matches the burned-in captions 'השבוע הגיע אמא למיון עם ילדה', 'מאוד מאוד מיובשת', 'מזיעה', 'ובאמת עם התייבשות').
beats.on_screen_text: השבוע הגיע אמא למיון עם ילדה / מאוד מאוד מיובשת, / מזיעה, / ובאמת עם התייבשות, (This week a mom came to the ER with a girl / very very dehydrated, / sweating, / and truly dehydrated)

beats.observed: Same framing; she gestures with open hands and explains the cause. The cloth on the stroller is the only prop.
beats.spoken: The simple reason: she walked with her in the park and put some kind of tetra-type cloth over the stroller (Whisper; 'תהילה' is likely 'טיילה', walked, my inference).
beats.on_screen_text: מהסיבה הפשוטה / ברחוב בפארק ושמה / לה איזשהוא חיתול (For the simple reason / in the street in the park and put / on it some kind of cloth/diaper)

beats.observed: She points to the stroller with her hands wide; caption words continue in sync.
beats.spoken: A tetra cloth on the stroller, and basically all the heat stays inside and the girl got dehydrated.
beats.on_screen_text: טטרא בזה על העגלה, / ובעצם כל החום / נשאר בפנים והילדה / התייבשה, (tetra cloth on the stroller, / and basically all the heat / stays inside and the girl / got dehydrated)

beats.observed: She leans in and speaks directly to the camera with hand gestures.
beats.spoken: So it is important to know that a child needs air much more than shade, so do not do this thing.
beats.on_screen_text: אז חשוב שתדעו / שהילד צריך אוויר / הרבה יותר מצל, / אז לא לעשות את / הדבר הזה. (So it is important that you know / that the child needs air / much more than shade, / so do not do / this thing.)

beats.observed: She keeps eye contact with the camera, hands together in front of her; the caption gives the ask in three chunks.
beats.spoken: And send this to friends and to young mothers and also to fathers so they know this is very dangerous.
beats.on_screen_text: ותשלחו את זה לחברות / ולאמהות צעירות / וגם לאבות כדי / שידעו שזה דבר / מאוד מסוכן. (and send this to friends / and to young mothers / and also to fathers so / they know this is a thing / very dangerous.)

beats.observed: She stays in frame looking at the camera with hands together and no caption showing, then the video ends.

payoff: The rule arrives at about 18.5 to 25.5 s ('a child needs air much more than shade, so do not do this'); the explicit 'send it to friends, young mothers and fathers' ask follows at 26 to 33 s.
cta: Send the video to friends, young mothers and also fathers (spoken and captioned, 26 to 33 s). The post caption restates the rule.
share_or_comment_trigger: A safety warning about a habit parents recognise, plus an explicit instruction naming three audiences to forward it to. 221 comments suggest parents also respond with their own experience or doubts (inferred; I have not read the comments).
why_it_worked: 842,752 views, 4.0x her own median of 211,117: a strong account, and this post beat it with a 0.72% like rate and 221 comments.
Credible clinical voice (scrubs, 'this week in the ER') and a vivid cause-and-effect story in the first 18 s, delivered in plain spoken Hebrew with word-highlight captions.

A one-line rule (air matters more than shade) and a named-audience share ask in the last 10 s. The low like rate relative to views is typical of warning content that is forwarded rather than liked (inferred; shares are not in the data).
paid_signal: no, like rate is 0.72%, above the 0.3% level, and 4.0x outlier on a large organic account is unremarkable.

solo_route.how: 1) Recruit a barter expert (pediatric nurse, speech therapist or occupational therapist) in exchange for a LumeBook, and ask them for a REAL recent case or common mistake from their work: do not script a clinical anecdote for them. 2) Give them the four-part skeleton: this week I saw X, because of Y, so the rule is Z, send this to a new parent. 3) They film selfie-style in their work clothes at a relevant location with one simple prop in frame (the stroller served this role). 4) You edit: Hebrew auto-captions in CapCut with the current-word highlight box, proofread every word because auto-Hebrew mishears, and add the ask in the caption.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert with credentials who supplies the real story and approves the claim. A 24-year-old with no kids cannot credibly deliver this herself, and invented medical anecdotes should not be posted.

lumebook_version.hook_he: קלינאית תקשורת: זו הטעות שאני רואה הכי הרבה בקריאת סיפור לילד
lumebook_version.concept: A 30 s selfie clip by a barter child-development expert: one real mistake she sees in bedtime reading, the one-line rule that fixes it, and 'send this to a friend who just became a parent', with LumeBook shown only in the caption or a pinned comment.

evidence_notes: Observed: scrubs, lanyard, the cloth-covered stroller visible throughout, burned-in Hebrew captions with a black highlight box on the current words, no child visible. Spoken: Whisper Hebrew is good but mishears the opening ('בוא יגיע' vs the burned-in 'השבוע הגיע') and 'תהילה' (likely 'טיילה'); the burned-in captions are the reliable text. The frames do not prove anything about dehydration or the danger: the clinical claim, and the story about a patient, are the speaker's own statements and the caption's. The account name says pediatric ER nurse; I did not verify credentials. In the caption on screen the word reads 'טטרא בזה', quoted exactly as seen. Meta duration is null, but frames/index.json gives 35.1 s. Shares are not in meta.json.
